set.acceptance: make -n test-budgets shows the timing budgets run alone, -count=1 -p 1, one package at a time, and make -n test runs none of them (@{01M7EQDFY7GKPF549RAPQE285W})
set.statement: The timing budgets are opt-in benchmarks: make test runs the suite with them skipped, and make test-budgets runs them alone, -count=1 -p 1 one package at a time, printing the read-budget timings; CI's budgets job runs make test-budgets on every pull request, so no budget test is lost.

fields.acceptance: make -n test shows go test with -skip of the budget tests and no -run of them, and no budget phase; make -n test-budgets shows them run -count=1 -p 1 over the packages that hold them; every name in BUDGET_TESTS matches a test that go test -list finds (TestGeneratedModel is dropped or found); go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run '^(TestMakeTestTimeout|TestMakeTestShardTargets|TestMakeUpdateDryRun)$' passes with its expected commands updated; .github/workflows/ci.yml's budgets job still runs make test-budgets; failure case: TestMakeTestShardTargets fails when make test's recipe runs a budget test. Speedup measure (orchestrator, quiet VM): a warm /usr/bin/time -f '%e s' make test, against 254 s, with no 'Timing budgets' phase in its output. Touches Makefile, cmd/rhiza/makeupdate_test.go, AGENTS.md. Must not drop a budget test from test-budgets or change a budget limit.
fields.statement: make test and make check no longer run the timing budgets: the budget phase leaves make test's recipe, the budgets run only in the opt-in make test-budgets (alone, -count=1 -p 1, printing the read-budget timings), which CI's budgets job runs on every pull request, and AGENTS.md and the Makefile's comments say so.
